_readme: Owned by Agent B (task B3b). Agent A wrote the two entries below as the §7 fallback
so A5 was not blocked; overwrite them freely, the assembler does not care.
Keys MUST be finding IDs from contract/types.ts FINDING_IDS. A snippet whose ID is
not in the generated project's appliedFindingIds is skipped, so it is safe to ship
snippets for findings that only some option combinations mitigate.
`body` lines are Solidity statements placed inside the test function at one indent.
`helpers` lines are emitted at contract level (extra helper contracts, constants).
Placeholders are substituted before emission; any {{UNKNOWN}} left over is a hard
error rather than a silently broken test.
A finding may have more than one snippet (e.g. one per preset). Key them
'<FINDING_ID>#<variant>'; everything before the '#' is the finding ID.

placeholders.{{CONTRACT}}: the deployed instance under test, e.g. `harness`
placeholders.{{CONTRACT_TYPE}}: the generated contract's type name, e.g. `MyFlashLoanReceiver`
placeholders.{{POOL}}: IPool, resolved from the addresses provider in setUp
placeholders.{{PARAMS}}: call to `_defaultParams()`, which abi.encodes a valid FlashParams
placeholders.{{PARAMS_STRUCT}}: call to `_defaultFlashParams()`, the same params unencoded
placeholders.{{OWNER}}: the authorised caller created in setUp
placeholders._note: Snippets may declare `presets`; omitted means both. A snippet is emitted only if its finding ID is in appliedFindingIds AND its preset matches.

AAVE-FL-001.title: Flash-loan callback not gated to Pool + initiator
comments: AAVE-FL-001 — anyone may call Pool.flashLoanSimple naming OUR contract as the
receiver. Aave then invokes our callback on their behalf, with their params.
Checking msg.sender == Pool is NOT enough: the Pool really is the caller.
This is the bug that drained DODO MarginTrading and Mimo SuperVault.

AAVE-FL-002.title: Attacker-controlled calldata executed from callback params
comments: AAVE-FL-002 — the tutorial pattern decodes `params` into (address target,
bytes data) and calls it, turning finding 001 from a revert into a drain.
Here `params` decodes to a fixed struct with no call target, so hostile bytes
cannot become an external call. Asserted even with both other gates satisfied.
body: // Worst case: the attacker somehow satisfies the caller AND initiator gates.

AAVE-FL-013.title: Idle funds held on the flash-loan receiver
comments: AAVE-FL-013 — a balance sitting on a receiver is repayment for somebody else's
flash loan. An attacker borrows, does nothing, and lets YOUR balance cover the
premium. The initiator gate is what stops it, so assert the balance survives.
body: "idle funds were consumed repaying someone else's flash loan"

AAVE-SWP-014.title: Missing minAmountOut on the swap leg

incidents.name: vuln/defi/slippage — 120 tagged PoCs in the registry

comments: AAVE-SWP-014 — a swap leg with no floor on output is a free sandwich. The
contract refuses to proceed rather than trusting the caller to pass one.

AAVE-RISK-010.title: Supply/borrow cap and pause reverts unhandled
comments: AAVE-RISK-010 — caps, freezes and pauses make Aave revert mid-flow, and a
leverage loop that ignores them bricks. Halting must be a clean revert that
leaves no partial state, and must be reversible.
body: // No bricked state: unpausing restores normal operation.

AAVE-VLT-009.title: No ERC20 escape hatch for airdrops / stuck tokens
comments: AAVE-VLT-009 — Merkl rewards, airdrops and dust arrive unannounced. Without a
hatch they are stuck forever; with an ungated one, anyone drains the contract.
Both halves are asserted here.

AAVE-VLT-003.title: aToken.balanceOf used as share-price denominator
comments: AAVE-VLT-003 — aTokens are ordinary transferable ERC20s, so a donation needs
no interaction with Aave at all. A vault whose totalAssets() reads the aToken
balance lets anyone move the share price for the next depositor, for free.
body: // Mint real aTokens, then hand them straight to the vault.
assertEq({{CONTRACT}}.convertToAssets(1e6), priceBefore, "share price moved on a free donation");

AAVE-VLT-004.title: Aave withdraw() return value ignored
comments: AAVE-VLT-004 — Aave's withdraw returns the amount ACTUALLY withdrawn, which is
less than requested when the reserve is illiquid, capped, frozen or paused.
Crediting the requested amount instead silently mints value out of nothing.

AAVE-VLT-011.title: ERC-4626 receiver and owner conflated
comments: AAVE-VLT-011 — redeem(shares, receiver, owner) burns from `owner` and pays
`receiver`. Mixing the two burns Alice's shares and pays Bob, or worse.
body: // Alice redeems her own shares but directs the assets to Bob.
assertEq(IERC20({{ASSET}}).balanceOf(alice), 0, "assets went to the owner, not the receiver");

AAVE-VLT-009#vault.title: No ERC20 escape hatch for airdrops / stuck tokens
comments: AAVE-VLT-009 — a vault needs a hatch for airdrops, but a hatch that can reach
the principal or its aToken is not a hatch, it is the vulnerability.

AAVE-VLT-008.title: RewardsController rewards permanently unclaimable
comments: AAVE-VLT-008 — Aave base yield is not incentives. Without a claim path the
emissions are lost; with an ungated one, anyone redirects them.
body: // Emissions may legitimately be zero at this block. What is asserted is that a
// claim path exists at all and that only the operator can drive it.

AAVE-RISK-010#vault.title: Supply/borrow cap and pause reverts unhandled
comments: AAVE-RISK-010 — caps, freezes and pauses make Aave revert mid-flow. Halting
must be clean and reversible, leaving no partial state behind.

AAVE-RISK-006.title: LTV-0 aToken poison dust can freeze withdrawals

incidents.name: StErMi — Aave v3 LTV-0 bug bounty

comments: AAVE-RISK-006 — one wei of a zero-LTV aToken, sent by anyone, must not brick
redemptions. aTokens are ordinary transferable ERC20s, so this grief costs the
attacker a single wei and there is no permissionless way to push it back out.
The aTokens are acquired by genuinely supplying to Aave: aToken balances are
scaled, so a forged `deal` balance would not behave like a real transfer.
body: assertGt(received, 0, "1 wei of zero-LTV aToken bricked redemptions");

AAVE-RISK-006#receiver.title: LTV-0 aToken poison dust can freeze withdrawals

incidents.name: StErMi — Aave v3 LTV-0 bug bounty

comments: AAVE-RISK-006 — anyone can push a zero-LTV aToken onto this contract. It must
stay inert: the callback gates keep holding and the dust cannot be leveraged
by whoever sent it.
body: // The dust must not become a lever for a third-party flash loan.
"zero-LTV dust changed the contract's Aave position"
